title: Stock Market Highlights, November 25: Sensex surges 1,502 points, Nifty reclaims 25,800 as rupee hits eight-month high - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: Find here all the updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 25th November 2026.

CLOSING BELL: Indian equity markets staged a strong rebound on Wednesday, with the Sensex surging 1,502.29 points or 1.82 per cent to 83,938.28 and the Nifty gaining 469.60 points or 1.85 per cent to close at 25,819.25. Fresh buying in heavyweight stocks, sustained foreign investor inflows, easing crude oil prices and a stronger rupee lifted sentiment.

FMCG led sectoral gains, followed by private banks, pharma and financial services, while metal, media, chemicals, realty and telecom stocks faced selling pressure. Hindustan Unilever, IndiGo, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and ITC were among the leading gainers, while Bharti Airtel and Tata Steel weighed on the indices.

The rupee strengthened 0.7 per cent to 92.23 against the US dollar, touching an eight-month high of 92.1850.

Analysts expect near-term consolidation, identifying 26,000 as the Nifty’s immediate resistance and 25,500–25,350 as an important support zone.

Sensex rallies 1,502 points: The BSE benchmark surged 1.82 per cent to close at 83,938.28.

Nifty reclaims 25,800: The NSE benchmark gained 469.60 points or 1.85 per cent to settle at 25,819.25.

FMCG leads sectoral rally: Nifty FMCG emerged as the top-performing sector, gaining 3.79 per cent.

Heavyweights drive gains: Hindustan Unilever, IndiGo, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, ITC and Reliance were among the major contributors.

Foreign inflows support sentiment: Foreign investors pumped over $14 billion into Indian equities so far in November, according to Religare Broking.

Rupee hits eight-month high: The domestic currency appreciated 0.7 per cent to close at 92.23 against the US dollar, taking its November gains to 2.9 per cent.

Crude oil prices ease: Lower oil prices improved sentiment amid expectations of relief on India’s import bill and inflation.

Market breadth remains mixed: Metal, media, chemicals, realty and telecom indices ended lower, while most other sectoral indices advanced.

Nifty faces 26,000 hurdle: Analysts see immediate resistance at 25,900–26,000, with a sustained breakout potentially opening the way to 26,300–26,400.

Consolidation likely: Analysts expect the Nifty to consolidate in the 25,000–26,300 range in the near term, with support around 25,500–25,350.

The Indian rupee returned with renewed momentum after a day’s gap, climbing to its highest level so far ‌this financial year, as strong foreign inflows to India’s stock market lent ⁠support.

The rupee opened higher at 92.74 per US dollar, after dropping to 92.91 on Monday. It extended ‌gains through the session to hit an eight-month high of 92.1850.

The currency ‌ended 0.7% higher for the day ‌at ⁠92.23, pushing its gains in November up ⁠to 2.9%. Indian financial markets were shut on Tuesday for a holiday.

Vikram Kasat - Chief Business Officer – Advisory and Dealing at PL Capital

“The sharp rebound in Indian equities reflects improving investor confidence, supported by sustained foreign inflows and easing crude prices. However, the rally remains selective, with FMCG and private banking gaining 2.88% and 2.14%, respectively, while metals and media declined 2.45% and 4.54%. The weakness in midcaps and smallcaps further suggests that investors continue to favour established large-cap businesses. The rupee’s appreciation to ₹92.42 against the US dollar and Brent crude easing to around $90.10 per barrel provide additional macroeconomic comfort. Meanwhile, MCX gold and silver traded around ₹1,21,961 per 10 grams and ₹1,44,795 per kg, while crude oil and natural gas were around ₹7,476 per barrel and ₹344.70 per MMBtu, respectively. FIIs bought ₹5,673 crore, while DIIs sold ₹2,760 crore in the previous session. Going ahead, earnings visibility and sustained inflows will be key; we favour selective accumulation over chasing momentum.”
